title: What shifts threshold distributions in social contagions?
abstract: arXiv:2510.04785v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Individual thresholds in social contagions capture what fraction of others must adopt a new product or behavior before an individual adopts it. Yet in a given choice context and population, we rarely know the empirical threshold distribution or what explains its heterogeneity. This limits the ability to predict diffusion dynamics and design effective network interventions. We address this by measuring thresholds with an incentivized online experiment in which participants make adoption decisions for products that vary in attractiveness and payoff uncertainty. The results show that product characteristics shift threshold distributions: lower attractiveness and higher uncertainty increase thresholds. Individual characteristics, however, remain essential for explaining threshold heterogeneity. translated_title: 什么改变了社会传染中的阈值分布？
translated_abstract: 社会传染中的个体阈值刻画了在个体采纳一种新产品或行为之前，需要有多大比例的其他人先行采纳。然而，在给定的选择情境和人群中，我们很少知道实际的阈值分布，也不清楚是什么因素解释了其异质性，这限制了预测扩散动力学和设计有效网络干预的能力。我们通过一项有激励的在线实验来测量阈值，实验中参与者需要对吸引力和收益不确定性各不相同的产品做出采纳决策。结果表明，产品特征会改变阈值分布：较低的吸引力和较高的不确定性会提高阈值。然而，个体特征对于解释阈值异质性仍然至关重要。随后，我们利用数据驱动的模拟表明，产品特征和个体特征均会调节长期……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究通过有激励的在线实验与数据驱动模拟发现，社会传染中的采纳阈值分布同时受产品特征（吸引力越低、不确定性越高，阈值越高）和个体特征的共同调节。
en_tdlr: Using an incentivized online experiment and data-driven simulations, this paper shows that threshold distributions in social contagions are shifted by both product characteristics (lower attractiveness and higher uncertainty raise thresholds) and individual characteristics.
